lines.text: ’Tis past the hour, sir, that Sir Hugh promised to meet.

blocks.text: By gar, he has save his soul, dat he is no come; he has pray his Pible vell dat he is no come: by gar, Jack Rugby, he is dead already, if he be come.

lines.text: He is wise, sir; he knew your worship would kill him if he came.

blocks.text: By gar, de herring is no dead so as I vill kill him. Take your rapier, Jack; I vill tell you how I vill kill him.

lines.text: Villany, take your rapier. They begin to fence.

blocks.text: Enter Host, Justice Shallow, Slender, and Page.

lines.text: Vat be all you, one, two, tree, four, come for?

blocks.text: To see thee fight, to see thee foin, to see thee traverse; to see thee here, to see thee there; to see thee pass thy punto, thy stock, thy reverse, thy distance, thy montant. Is he dead, my Ethiopian? Is he dead, my Francisco? Ha, bully! What says my Aesculapius? my Galen? my heart of elder? Ha! is he dead, bully stale? Is he dead?

lines.text: By gar, he is de coward Jack priest of de world; he is not show his face.
Thou art a Castalion King Urinal! Hector of Greece, my boy!

blocks.text: I pray you, bear witness that me have stay six or seven, two, tree hours for him, and he is no come.
He is the wiser man, Master doctor: he is a curer of souls, and you a curer of bodies; if you should fight, you go against the hair of your professions. Is it not true, Master Page?
Master Shallow, you have yourself been a great fighter, though now a man of peace.

Bodykins, Master Page, though I now be old, and of the peace, if I see a sword out, my finger itches to make one. Though we are justices, and doctors, and churchmen, Master Page, we have some salt of our youth in us; we are the sons of women, Master Page.

It will be found so, Master Page. Master Doctor Caius, I come to fetch you home. I am sworn of the peace; you have showed yourself a wise physician, and Sir Hugh hath shown himself a wise and patient churchman. You must go with me, Master Doctor.

lines.text: Mockwater, in our English tongue, is valour, bully.

blocks.text: By gar, then I have as much mockvater as de Englishman.⁠—Scurvy jack-dog priest! By gar, me vill cut his ears.

lines.text: He will clapperclaw thee tightly, bully.
That is, he will make thee amends.
By gar, me do look he shall clapper-de-claw me; for, by gar, me vill have it.
And I will provoke him to’t, or let him wag.

blocks.text: And, moreover, bully⁠—aside but first: Master guest, and Master Page, and eke Cavaliero Slender, go you through the town to Frogmore.

lines.text: Sir Hugh is there, is he?

blocks.text: He is there: see what humour he is in; and I will bring the doctor about by the fields. Will it do well?
Exeunt Page, Justice Shallow, and Slender.

lines.text: By gar, me vill kill de priest; for he speak for a jack-an-ape to Anne Page.

blocks.text: Let him die. Sheathe thy impatience; throw cold water on thy choler; go about the fields with me through Frogmore; I will bring thee where Mistress Anne Page is, at a farmhouse a-feasting; and thou shalt woo her. Cried I aim! Said I well?
By gar, me tank you for dat: by gar, I love you; and I shall procure-a you de good guest, de earl, de knight, de lords, de gentlemen, my patients.

lines.text: For the which I will be thy adversary toward Anne Page: said I well?
Come at my heels, Jack Rugby.
